questions.question: Which of the following Constitutional Amendment Acts added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**52nd Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 52nd Amendment Act of 1985 added the 10th Schedule to the Indian Constitution.
 
• The 10th Schedule is commonly known as the Anti-Defection Law.
 
• The Anti-Defection Law lays down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection.
 
• This amendment aimed to address the issue of political defections by legislators, which were becoming a common problem in Indian politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Defection:**

 
 
• Defection refers to the act of a member of a legislative body leaving their political party to join another.
 
• The Anti-Defection Law was introduced to prevent such political defections.
 
 
 
• **Disqualification:**
 
 
• The 10th Schedule outlines the grounds for disqualification of legislators on the grounds of defection.
 
• A legislator can be disqualified if they voluntarily give up the membership of their party or disobey the party's directives.
 
 
 
• **Exceptions:**
 
 
• The law allows for certain exceptions, such as mergers between parties.
 
• If a party merges with another and two-thirds of its legislators agree, they are not considered to have defected.
 
 
 
• **Authority:**
 
 
• The presiding officer of the house (Speaker or Chairman) is the authority to decide on disqualification matters under the 10th Schedule.
 
• However, the decision of the presiding officer is subject to judicial review.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution deals with the separation of judiciary from the executive?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Article 50**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 50** of the Indian Constitution is part of the Directive Principles of State Policy. It aims to separate the judiciary from the executive in the public services of the State to ensure independence.
 
• This separation is crucial for **upholding the integrity** of the judiciary and avoiding any influence or bias from the executive branch of the government.
 
• The objective is to maintain the **rule of law** and ensure a fair and impartial judicial process for all citizens.
 
• Article 50 is not enforceable by courts, as it is a directive principle, but it guides the governance of the country to establish a system where the judiciary operates independently of the executive branch.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
 

 Option
 Details
 
 

 Article 53
 Specifies the executive power of the Union vested in the President and exercised directly or through officers subordinate to him.
 
 

 Article 52
 Establishes the office of the President of India as the head of the Executive of the Union.
 
 

 Article 51
 Deals with the promotion of international peace and security, encouraging respect for international law, and treaty obligations.

questions.question: Which key feature of Thomson’s Atomic Model helped explain the electrical neutrality of an atom?

options.text: The nucleus contained both, protons and neutrons
The positive charge was concentrated in the centre.
The positive and negative charges are equal in magnitude.
Electrons revolved around the nucleus in fixed orbits.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The positive and negative charges are equal in magnitude**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Thomson's atomic model**, also known as the "plum pudding model," proposed that an atom consists of a positively charged sphere with negatively charged electrons embedded in it.
 
• The model explained electrical neutrality by asserting that the **total positive and negative charges in an atom are equal in magnitude**, thereby balancing each other.
 
• Electrons, being negatively charged, were uniformly distributed throughout the positively charged "pudding," ensuring no net charge on the atom.
 
• This model laid the foundation for understanding the structure of atoms and their neutrality, despite its inability to explain atomic stability or spectral lines.
 
• The concept of equal positive and negative charges was a significant step toward uncovering the atomic structure, leading to further advancements in atomic theory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: The nucleus contained both, protons and neutrons**

 
 
• This statement is incorrect in the context of Thomson's model because his model did not include the concept of a nucleus. The idea of a nucleus was introduced later by Rutherford.
 
• Protons and neutrons being located in the nucleus was established through Rutherford's and Chadwick's contributions, making this statement irrelevant to Thomson's theory.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: The positive charge was concentrated in the centre**
 
 
• This statement aligns with Rutherford's nuclear model, not Thomson's atomic model.
 
• In Rutherford's model, the atom was visualized as having a dense, positively charged nucleus at the center, surrounded by electrons. Thomson's model, in contrast, assumed a uniform distribution of positive charge.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Electrons revolved around the nucleus in fixed orbits**
 
 
• This concept is a feature of Bohr's atomic model, not Thomson's model.
 
• Bohr proposed that electrons travel in fixed orbits around the nucleus, explaining atomic stability and spectral lines, which Thomson's model could not address.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Thomson's Atomic Model**
 
 
• Thomson's atomic model was the first attempt to describe the internal structure of an atom.
 
• Though it was eventually replaced by more advanced models, it played a crucial role in shaping the early understanding of atomic structure.

questions.question: In 1 minute how much energy does a 100 W electric bulb transfers?
questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**Energy and Power Relationship**

__
 
• Energy transferred by an electrical device is related to its power and time of operation.
 
• Power (P) is defined as the rate at which energy is transferred or used.
 
• The formula to calculate energy transferred is:
 
Energy (E) = Power (P) × Time (t)

 
 
• In this formula:
 
 
• Energy (E) is measured in joules (J).
 
• Power (P) is measured in watts (W).
 
• Time (t) is measured in seconds (s).
 
 

**EXPLANATION**__:

__
 
• In the given problem:
 
 
• Power of the bulb (P) = 100 W
 
• Time (t) = 1 minute = 60 seconds
 
 
 
• Using the formula for energy:
 
 
• E = P × t
 
• E = 100 × 60
 
• E = 6000 J
 
 

**Therefore, the energy transferred by a 100 W electric bulb in 1 minute is 6000 J__.**

questions.question: How was the structure of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rectangle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Great Bath of Mohenjo-daro is one of the most famous structures found at the site of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization.
 
• It is a large, rectangular tank located in the citadel area, which suggests its importance for ritualistic or ceremonial purposes.
 
• The tank measures approximately 12 meters long, 7 meters wide, and 2.4 meters deep.
 
• The structure is made of finely fitted bricks and features a series of steps leading down to the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mohenjo-daro**

 
 
• Mohenjo-daro is one of the largest settlements of the ancient Indus Valley Civilization, located in present-day Sindh, Pakistan.
 
• The name Mohenjo-daro means "Mound of the Dead" in Sindhi.
 
• The city was built around 2500 BCE and is known for its advanced urban planning and architecture.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**
 
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization was one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, contemporaneous with the civilizations of ancient Egypt and Mesopotamia.
 
• It flourished in the basins of the Indus River, which flows through present-day Pakistan and northwest India.
 
• The civilization is noted for its cities built of brick, roadside drainage systems, and multi-story houses.
 
 
 
• **Archaeological Significance**
 
 
• The Great Bath is considered one of the earliest public water tanks in the ancient world.
 
• Its construction techniques, such as the use of bitumen for waterproofing, highlight the advanced engineering skills of the Indus Valley people.

questions.question: Which space mission launched by NASA aims to map the heliosphere’s boundary, track energetic particles, and enhance space weather forecasting?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **NASA launched the Interstellar Mapping and Acceleration Probe (IMAP)__ to map the heliosphere’s boundary and enhance space weather forecasting.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The mission explores the heliosphere__, the Sun’s protective bubble, and its interaction with interstellar space.**
 
• **IMAP is positioned at the __Earth-Sun Lagrange Point 1 (L1)__ to provide an optimal vantage point for observation.**
 
• **The spacecraft uses __10 instruments__ to study solar wind, energetic particles, magnetic fields, and cosmic remnants.**
 
• **The mission aims to uncover how solar particles are energized and how the heliosphere shields Earth from galactic radiation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heliosphere**__

 __
 
• The bubble of charged particles and magnetic fields surrounding the Sun and the solar system.
 
• Protects Earth from galactic cosmic radiation.
 
 
 
• **Lagrange Point L1**__
 __
 
• A point in space where the gravitational forces of the Earth and Sun balance the centripetal force felt by a satellite.
 
• Positioned about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, ideal for observing solar wind and space weather.
 
 
 
• **Space Weather Forecasting**__
 __
 
• IMAP provides real-time data to monitor and predict space weather, which is crucial for protecting astronauts and Earth-based technologies.
 
 
 
• **IMAP's Scientific Goals**__
 
 
• Study solar wind interactions with interstellar medium.
 
• Understand cosmic radiation effects and planetary habitability.

questions.question: _______ refers to the physical arrangement of network components and media within an enterprise network structure.
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Internet surfing** as it is popularly known is moving from page to page on the Internet, browsing for topics of interest.

questions.question: Name the scientist who discovered neutron?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chadwick**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **James Chadwick**, an English physicist, is credited with the discovery of the **neutron** in 1932.
 
• He performed a series of experiments where he bombarded beryllium atoms with alpha particles, leading to the emission of neutral radiation, later identified as neutrons.
 
• Chadwick's discovery of the neutron provided a deeper understanding of the atomic nucleus and explained the existence of isotopes.
 
• His work was pivotal in advancing nuclear science, including the development of nuclear reactors and atomic bombs during World War II.
 
• In recognition of his groundbreaking discovery, he was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Physics in 1935**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bohr:**

 
 
• Niels Bohr was a Danish physicist who proposed the **Bohr model of the atom** in 1913.
 
• His model introduced the concept of electrons orbiting the nucleus in fixed energy levels, explaining atomic spectra.
 
• Bohr’s contributions laid the foundation for quantum mechanics and modern atomic theory.
 
 
 
• **Rutherford:**
 
 
• Ernest Rutherford, known as the "Father of Nuclear Physics," discovered the **nucleus of the atom** in 1911 through his gold foil experiment.
 
• He proposed that the atom consists of a small, dense nucleus surrounded by electrons, forming the basis of the nuclear model of the atom.
 
• He also discovered the concept of radioactive half-life and identified alpha and beta radiation.
 
 
 
• **Thomson:**
 
 
• J.J. Thomson was an English physicist who discovered the **electron** in 1897 through experiments with cathode rays.
 
• He proposed the "plum pudding model" of the atom, where electrons were embedded in a positively charged "pudding."
 
• Although later replaced by Rutherford’s model, Thomson’s discovery of the electron was a key milestone in atomic science.

questions.question: Acid rain will occur when the pH of rain water is less than _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.6**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Acid rain will occur when the pH of rainwater is less than **5.6**.
 
• Normal rainwater has a pH of about **5.6** due to the natural presence of carbon dioxide, which forms carbonic acid.
 
• A pH level below **5.6** indicates the presence of stronger acids such as sulfuric and nitric acids, which result from industrial pollution.
 
• Acid rain can cause significant environmental damage, affecting aquatic life, soil chemistry, and plant life.
 
• It is primarily caused by emissions of sulfur dioxide (SO₂) and nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) from burning fossil fuels.

questions.question: The process to divide disk into track & sector is ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Formatting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Formatting** is the process of preparing a data storage device such as a hard drive, solid-state drive, or USB flash drive for initial use.
 
• During the formatting process, the disk is divided into **tracks** and **sectors**.
 
• Tracks are concentric circles on the disk's surface, while sectors are pie-shaped wedges that divide each track into smaller segments.
 
• Formatting can be **low-level (physical) formatting**, which sets up the tracks and sectors, or **high-level (logical) formatting**, which creates the file system structure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **File System:**

 
 
• A file system is a method and data structure that an operating system uses to control how data is stored and retrieved.
 
• Common file systems include NTFS, FAT32, and exFAT for Windows, and ext4 for Linux.
 
 
 
• **Partition:**
 
 
• A partition is a logical division of a hard drive, allowing one physical disk to be divided into multiple sections that can be managed separately.
 
• Each partition can be formatted with a different file system.
 
 
 
• **Low-Level Formatting:**
 
 
• Also known as physical formatting, this process creates the physical structure of the disk by setting up tracks and sectors.
 
• It is usually performed at the factory before the disk is sold.
 
 
 
• **High-Level Formatting:**
 
 
• Also known as logical formatting, this process creates the file system structure, allowing the operating system to manage files and directories.
 
• This is the type of formatting most users perform when preparing a disk for use.

questions.question: Which substance is used to prevent rusting of iron in galvanisation process?
questions.solution:
**__Explanation:__**

**Galvanisation Process**

 
• Galvanisation is a process of coating a metal, typically iron or steel, with a layer of zinc.
 
• This layer of zinc acts as a protective barrier and prevents the iron underneath from rusting.
 
• The zinc coating protects the iron both physically (by acting as a shield) and chemically (by corroding in preference to the iron, a process known as sacrificial protection).
 
 
• Aluminium, copper, and magnesium are not typically used in the galvanisation process.
 
• Zinc is the standard and widely used substance for galvanisation, as it provides effective protection against rusting and corrosion.
 
 

 
• Zinc forms a protective layer of zinc oxide and zinc carbonate when it reacts with oxygen and carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, further enhancing its rust-resistant properties.

**Therefore, the correct answer is Zinc.**

questions.question: At which place did Gandhiji deliver the "do or die" slogan during the Quit India Movement?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Bombay**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Quit India Movement**: The Quit India Movement, also known as the Bharat Chodo Andolan, was a significant movement in the Indian independence struggle. It was launched in August 1942, during World War II, under the leadership of Mahatma Gandhi and the Indian National Congress.
 
• **Gandhiji's Role**: Mahatma Gandhi played a pivotal role in this movement. He was the main architect behind its strategy and its moral and ideological leader. Gandhi advocated for a non-violent struggle and civil disobedience against British rule in India.
 
• **"Do or Die" Slogan**: The slogan "Do or Die" was coined by Gandhi during the Quit India Movement to motivate the Indian populace to fight for their freedom with all their might and not to retreat under any circumstance. It was a call to action for the people of India to either achieve freedom (do) or die in the attempt, emphasizing the urgency and the critical nature of the struggle for independence.
 
• **Location of the Speech**: Gandhi delivered the iconic "Do or Die" speech in Bombay (now Mumbai) at the Gowalia Tank Maidan, which has since been renamed August Kranti Maidan to commemorate the movement and the speech. This place became a historical landmark due to its association with the Quit India Movement and Gandhi's stirring call to the nation.
 
• **Significance of Bombay**: Bombay, being a major urban center and a key port city, was strategically important for the British. It was also a hub for the Indian freedom movement, where leaders could rally support from a large and diverse population. Gandhi's choice of Bombay for delivering his pivotal speech was symbolic and practical, aimed at garnering maximum national and international attention.
 
• **Outcome of the Movement**: Although the Quit India Movement was met with severe repression from the British government, leading to the arrest of many leaders including Gandhi himself, it marked a significant shift in the Indian independence struggle. It demonstrated the determination of the Indian people and significantly weakened the British hold on India, setting the stage for post-war negotiations that eventually led to independence in 1947.
 
• In summary, Gandhi's "Do or Die" speech delivered in Bombay during the Quit India Movement was a defining moment in the Indian independence struggle, symbolizing the resolve and sacrifice of the Indian people in their fight against British colonial rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-cooperation Movement in 1920 as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British rule in India through non-violent means or "Ahimsa".
 
• It was a mass protest against the British government's oppressive policies and aimed to attain self-governance or Swaraj.
 
• Gandhi urged people to withdraw their children from government schools, boycott British goods, resign from government employment, and refuse to pay taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• A tragic incident that took place on April 13, 1919, in Amritsar, where British troops fired on a large crowd of unarmed Indian protesters, causing hundreds of deaths.
 
• This event marked a turning point in Indian nationalism and galvanized the Indian population against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**
 
 
• An oppressive legislation passed by the British government in 1919 giving them the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• The act faced widespread opposition and was one of the catalysts for the Non-cooperation Movement.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj:**
 
 
• A term used to describe self-governance or "self-rule," which was the ultimate goal of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Gandhi's vision of Swaraj included not just political independence but also social and economic empowerment of the common people.
 
 
 
• **Ahimsa:**
 
 
• A principle of non-violence which is central to Gandhi's philosophy and strategy for the independence movement.
 
• Gandhi believed that non-violence was the most powerful weapon for oppressed people to achieve freedom and justice.

questions.question: Who won the Miss Universe 2025 title in Thailand?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Miss Mexico.**__

questions.question: Some bacteria are photosynthetic. Where are the photosynthetic pigments located in these cells?

options.text: In the infolding of the plasma membrane

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In the infolding of the plasma membrane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Photosynthetic bacteria, such as cyanobacteria, have their photosynthetic pigments located in the infoldings of the plasma membrane.
 
• These infoldings are known as thylakoids, which house pigments like chlorophyll a and phycobiliproteins.
 
• The arrangement of these infoldings increases the surface area for light absorption and photosynthesis.
 
• Unlike plants, photosynthetic bacteria do not have chloroplasts, so their pigments are integrated into the plasma membrane itself.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thylakoids:** Membrane-bound compartments inside chloroplasts and cyanobacteria where photosynthesis occurs.
 
• **Cyanobacteria:** Also known as blue-green algae, these are a phylum of bacteria that obtain their energy through photosynthesis.
 
• **Chlorophyll a:** A type of chlorophyll that is the primary pigment involved in the photosynthesis of cyanobacteria and plants.
 
• **Phycobiliproteins:** Pigments found in cyanobacteria that assist in capturing light energy for photosynthesis.
 
• **Plasma Membrane:** The cell membrane that separates the interior of the cell from the outside environment, involved in various cellular processes including photosynthesis in bacteria.
